name: Pickled Duck With Mustard Sauce and Red Cabbage
author: Marian Burros

ingredients.raw: 1 ⅓ cups salt plus 1 ½ tablespoons

steps.text: Marinate ducks overnight in mixture of water, salt and sugar. Before cooking, drain and wash. Fill cavities with parsley and bay leaves. Season with pepper. Place in large roasting pan and roast at 450 degrees for 15 minutes.
Add stock to depth of one-quarter inch; lift ducks so stock can run underneath. Continue cooking 30 to 35 minutes, adding stock if necessary. Cool 15 minutes.
Slice breasts and thighs thinly so that there are a total of 20 slices. Reserve remaining duck for other uses.
To reheat, wrap stacked slices of duck in foil and place in warm oven for 20 minutes.
Serve with mustard sauce and red cabbage, and garnish with kale and gooseberries.

name: Pistachio Polenta Cake
author: Melissa Clark
description: Adapted from “I’ll Bring Dessert: Simple, Sweet Recipes for Every Occasion” by Benjamina Ebuehi (Quadrille, 2024), this lemon-flavored cake is both easy to make and very festive. It also happens to be gluten-free. You will need a food processor to grind the pistachios, but the cake batter can be mixed together with a whisk. Along with the grated lemon zest, a little chopped preserved lemon  adds a complex, salty-savory note, but feel free to leave it out for a more straightforward citrus flavor. This cake keeps well overnight if you want to bake it ahead of time (store it at room temperature).

ingredients.raw: 7 tablespoons/100 grams extra-virgin olive oil or grapeseed oil, plus more for greasing
ingredients.item: tablespoons/100 grams extra-virgin olive oil or grapeseed oil

ingredients.raw: 1 ½ cups/180 grams shelled pistachios, plus chopped pistachios to decorate the top
ingredients.preparation: plus chopped pistachios to decorate the top

ingredients.raw: ½ cup/80 grams fine-ground polenta or cornmeal
ingredients.item: cup/80 grams fine-ground polenta or cornmeal

ingredients.raw: 1 tablespoon finely chopped preserved lemon or use ½ teaspoon salt
ingredients.item: finely chopped preserved lemon or use ½ teaspoon salt

steps.text: Heat oven to 350 degrees. Grease an 8-inch cake pan, then line the bottom with parchment paper.
In a food processor, pulse the pistachios until finely ground. Add the polenta, sugar, baking soda and baking powder and pulse to combine.
In a large bowl, whisk together the eggs, 7 tablespoons oil, yogurt, preserved lemon (or salt) and lemon zest. Add pistachio mixture and fold to combine.

Pour batter into the prepared cake pan. Bake until the top is golden brown and a cake tester comes out clean, 25 to 35 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack to cool completely before glazing. Note that the cake will sink a bit in the middle as it cools.
To make the glaze, in a medium bowl, whisk together the powdered sugar and 1 tablespoon lemon juice. Continue whisking in more lemon juice as needed to yield a very thick but pourable glaze.
Spoon the glaze on the top of the cooled cake, using the back of a spoon to push it to the edges. Decorate top with chopped pistachios and let set for at least 30 minutes before serving.
